QuestionStmt.S: For a reaction to be spontaneous at all temperatures, the values of enthalpy change and entropy change should be

Solution.S:
For a reaction to be spontaneous, the Gibbs free energy change must be negative:

ΔG = ΔH - TΔS

For the reaction to be spontaneous at all temperatures, ΔG should remain negative for every value of T.

This is possible when ΔH < 0 (enthalpy term favours spontaneity) and ΔS > 0 (so -TΔS is also negative at all temperatures).

Thus, both terms in ΔG = ΔH - TΔS become negative, making ΔG negative at all temperatures.

Final Answer: $$\boxed{\text{ΔH < 0 and ΔS > 0}}$$

Hence, the correct option is B.
